meta.dataVersion: ERR 2.3.5.3 (mandude calculator regulation data) + ERR community wiki revisions up to 2026-11-01
meta.caveat: Public machine-readable ERR data stops at roughly 2.3.5.3-2.3.7.1; the mod is at 2.3.8.1 (Nexus, updated 30 Oct 2026). Numbers may have shifted in later patches. Treat values as close, not exact, and check in game.
meta.license: Text from the ELDEN RING Reforged community wiki (err.fandom.com) is CC BY-SA 3.0; attribute and share alike. Weapon numbers come from mandude/elden-ring-weapon-calculator (MIT). No ERR icons, images or other mod assets are included (the Nexus page forbids asset reuse).
meta.notes: ERR weapons (vanilla + new) with ERR scaling, requirements and attack from the 2.3.5.3 calculator data; errChanges and new-weapon descriptions from the ERR wiki. Armor sets keep the vanilla set list (vanilla Fextralife links for base stats) plus errSetPassive where the ERR wiki lists one. Talismans are the ERR wiki list (all weigh 0 in ERR). Scaling letters are the max-level values (ERR fixes scaling at max regardless of upgrade, except catalysts); scalingAtPlus0 is kept for catalysts. Crit is shown as stored in the calculator data (an offset; assumed displayed crit = 100 + value). Weapon locations are often empty: ERR moved items and the wiki has no full location table.

weapons.name: Albinauric Staff
weapons.description: Albinauric Staff (Glintstone Staff) in ELDEN RING Reforged. Numbers from the ERR calculator data (2.3.5.3).
weapons.location: Vanilla location (ERR may move items; check the ERR wiki): Found in Volcano Manor near the Guest Hall site of grace. Exit the room containing the grace, turn left, then turn left again, heading down the hall with the Caged Albinauric hanging from the ceiling. Go up both flights of stairs, then exit the building through the northern entrance, which is guarded by a Man-Serpent. Outside, make a left (west), then make another left where you will see a ladder leading onto the roof. Climb up the ladder, and then continuing straight ahead, you will see a ledge below, with an open doorway and lit lantern. Jump down onto the ledge and enter the room. The Albinauric Staff, along with the Albinauric Mask, is inside a room with an Omenkiller.

weapons.name: Bolt of Gransax
weapons.description: Founding incantation of the capital's ancient dragon cult. Creates a spear of red lightning and launches it forwards from above. On impact, the spear will burst into trails of lightning covering the area. A great ancient dragon, Gransax once rained calamity upon the Royal Capital - the only time in historical record that Leyndell's walls have fallen. This would inspire the creation of the capital's ancient dragon cult.
weapons.location: Vanilla location (ERR may move items; check the ERR wiki): Can be found in Leyndell, Royal Capital, after beating Godfrey, First Elden Lord (Golden Shade): From the Erdtree Sanctuary grace, walk out the western door, take the elevator down, go down the staircase to the walkway, jump down onto the giant spear lodged into the building, and then walk up it (you should see the Bolt shining near the handle of the giant spear).
weapons.errChanges:

weapons.name: Coilheart
weapons.description: Weapon once wielded by a gladiator in a past age. A paired set consisting of a broadsword and a serpentine shield. Inflicts poison buildup. A forked tongue tainted his will, coercing him to embrace cruelties he once rejected, in service to one he once thought just. The serpent's cinch is inescapable.
weapons.location:
To acquire Coilheart, you must first acquire the Gladius of Ophidion, the Coil Shield, and the Ringmaster Ophidion spirit ashes. 
Once acquired, put the Coil Shield in your left hand and the Gladius of Ophidion in your right hand. For the two to combine, you must summon Ringmaster Ophidion and have him perform his gesture. 
This can be done in a few different ways: you can summon him in any area with a spirit monument and then perform the Rallying Cry gesture while near him, or you can summon him in the Gilded Court (toggleable by interacting with the giant Spirit Monument behind the Rhyacis training dummy) and he will automatically perform the gesture upon aggroing onto you.
Upon obtaining Coilheart, you will permanently lose the Gladius of Ophidion and the Coil Shield, and will need to go to NG+ or use Starlight Tokens to get them again if desired.

weapons.description: Walking cane wrought from silver, with deadly function. Once wielded by a bookish Tarnished who fell from grace.  They honeyed words of a kindly deity sway even the most resolute of hearts. What hope, then, is there for one who strives for the betterment of his people?
weapons.location: The Gracebound Cane Sword is found in Elphael, just beyond the Elphael Inner Wall site of grace. Proceed down the hallway from the Rotten Crystalians and, instead of continuing through to the small rot swamp, keep going south, then look behind the large ornate chalice.

weapons.name: Gracebound Claws
weapons.description: Silver accessories of fine make, attached to one's fingers. Once wielded by a dour Tarnished who fell from grace.  Imbued with a resentful hex, these claws now slash with an otherworldly edge, drawn from the ire of their former master as she contends with her beloathed family in the spirit realm.
weapons.location:
The Gracebound Claws can be found at the base of a grave in the Mountaintops, in the graveyard with the Giant Skeletal Phantoms.
The player icon below marks the location.

weapons.name: Gracebound Dagger
weapons.description: Filigreed dagger bearing traces of magic. Once wielded by a refined Tarnished who fell from grace. The guidance of grace demands complete devotion, such that even familial bonds are abandoned in pursuit of lordship. The graves of the Gilded Court tell of how such fervor is rewarded.
weapons.location: The Gracebound Dagger can be found on a flower-adorned grave in the Gilded Court, found on the way to the Warrior's Rest.

source.label: mandude ELDEN RING Weapon Calculator data, Reforged v2.3.5.3 (MIT)

weapons.effects: Final hit of a light attack chain reprises damage upon enemies

weapons.name: Gracebound Greataxe
weapons.description: Colossal axe carved from a ship's figurehead. Once wielded by a mighty Tarnished who fell from grace.  Once dispersed across the Sea of Fog, some Tarnished would remain to plunder its waters, up until the call of grace brought them home to fight forevermore.
weapons.location: The Gracebound Greataxe can be found inside the Caelid Colosseum, accessed from behind the Great Jar. Walk inside and through the hallways to find it up against an altar.

source.label: mandude ELDEN RING Weapon Calculator data, Reforged v2.3.5.3 (MIT)

weapons.effects: Taking damage during skills increases skill power

weapons.name: Gracebound Greatshield
weapons.description: Artifact of a lost people, once wielded by a proud Tarnished who fell from grace. With the fall of the Storm King, a secretive people beholden to him is said to have left this realm. Though their storm arts persist upon the battlefield, few know their origins.
weapons.location: The Gracebound Greatshield is found after teleporting to the Crumbling Lands through the Four Belfries in Liurnia. It is located on a slanted pillar in the area with the two Beastmen of Farum Azula.

source.label: mandude ELDEN RING Weapon Calculator data, Reforged v2.3.5.3 (MIT)

weapons.effects: Guarding slowly heals self and nearby allies

weapons.name: Gracebound Greatsword
weapons.description: Eroded greatsword with a dulled edge. Once wielded by a knightly Tarnished who fell from grace.  Its blade is worn away by years of strife. Without its wielder's bloody work, there would be scores more adversaries for the Roundtable to face today.
weapons.location: The Gracebound Greatsword can be found at the edge of a cliff at the Church of Vengeance. The player icon is at the weapon's location.

source.label: mandude ELDEN RING Weapon Calculator data, Reforged v2.3.5.3 (MIT)

weapons.effects: Skill use coats armament in flame

weapons.name: Gracebound Halberd
weapons.description: Weathered halberd, hollowed like a bird's bones. Once wielded by a proud Tarnished who fell from grace.  The gales that swept around this halberd have worn away much of the fine metalwork that celebrates its heritage.
weapons.location: The Gracebound Halberd is found after teleporting to the Crumbling Lands through the Four Belfries in Liurnia. It is located on a slanted pillar in the area with the two Beastmen of Farum Azula.

source.label: mandude ELDEN RING Weapon Calculator data, Reforged v2.3.5.3 (MIT)

weapons.effects: Creates damaging whirlwind while charging attacks

weapons.name: Gracebound Katana
weapons.description: Blood-crusted sword from the Land of Reeds. Once wielded by a disciplined Tarnished who fell from grace.  The old blade bears the stains of a shameful suicide. Bad luck is sure to befall one who chooses to return this weapon to battle.
weapons.location:
The Gracebound Katana can be found in the Outer Wall Battleground in Altus Plateau. It is located in one of the many small craters with the enormous arrows sticking out, a little southeast of the Outer Wall Battleground site of grace. 
The player icon below marks the location.

weapons.name: Gracebound Longbow
weapons.description: Old oaken bow, wrapped with leather strips. Once wielded by a somber Tarnished who fell from grace.  The arrows loosed by this bow once felled the marks of a secretive order, rarely aligned with the Roundtable Hold. Such dual allegiances draw unwanted ire if not concealed.
weapons.location: The Gracebound Longbow can be found at the edge of the cliff just beyond the Abductor Virgin Duo in Volcano Manor, just before the drop down to the slanted rock that leads to Wyndham Ruins.

weapons.name: Gracebound Mace
weapons.description: Flanged mace wrought of black iron. Once wielded by a waifish Tarnished who fell from grace.  With a reputation for unsubtle bloodshed, one confessor soon lost the favor of the Two Fingers. In search for a cure to her compulsions, she followed the kindest of the demigods as long as she could.
weapons.location:
The Gracebound Mace can be found at a grave in the northwest of Charo's Hidden Grave, north of the location of the Furnace Golem.
The player icon below marks the location.

weapons.name: Gracebound Round Shield
weapons.description: Old wooden shield with flaking paint. Once wielded by a knightly Tarnished who fell from grace.  The white emblem upon a blue field reflects the culture of its wielder's distant origins. Its legacy persists despite his obscure demise.
weapons.location: The Gracebound Round Shield can be found at the edge of a cliff at the Church of Vengeance. The player icon is at the shield's location.

weapons.description: Staff fashioned from the living branch of a foreign tree. Once wielded by a tender Tarnished who fell from grace. weapons.location: The Gracebound Staff is found by a grave at the base of a large tree-like rock on the western side of the Consecrated Snowfield, south of the Apostate Derelict. The player icon below marks the location.

talismanGeneral:
All talismans now have zero weight.
All classes now start with 2 talisman slots. The third slot is unlocked upon defeating Margit, the Fell Omen, while the fourth slot is unlocked by speaking to Finger Reader Enia in Roundtable Hold after acquiring two Great Runes.
generalWeaponChanges:
=== Scaling ===
Armament attribute scaling (E to S+) no longer changes with armament reinforcement level but instead always uses the maximum scaling regardless of reinforcement. This means an armament with A scaling in Strength at +25 (or +10 for somber armaments) will also have A scaling at +0. This makes it easier to determine how a weapon will work within your build without any unnecessary guesswork. However, catalysts, including weapon catalysts, still increase their scaling with weapon level, as this is the only way to make them upgrade. 
The base damage of armaments has been reduced but their stat scaling has been greatly increased. This results in most of an armament's damage coming from your stats rather than smithing stones. Although both remain important for an armament to be fully effective. 
For characters investing incredibly heavily in bar stats (Vigor, Mind, and Endurance) and less in damage stats, it's recommended to experiment with status effects, as they deal percent health damage output and can make up for lower up-front damage. Crossbows are also largely stat agnostic. Additionally, Spirit Ashes can be a great asset to damage if you have the FP to consistently enrage them and the Mind to extend the duration of their rage. 
=== Two-handing ===
The 50% Strength damage boost from two-handing an armament has been removed, and replaced with a global 8% damage increase when doing so. This allows all melee armaments to benefit from two-handing. 
The 50% Strength boost when two-handing for the purpose of meeting minimum stat requirements still exists.
=== Catalyst Attacks ===
Catalysts have been reworked to have unique projectile based heavy attacks. 
All on hit effects such as affinity passives and status buildup on catalysts are applied via this heavy attack, not through spells. 
Many catalyst attacks are condensed versions of actual spells of the spell category the catalyst boosts or come with innately as a mystic ash skill, and share properties with those spells (ex: albinauric staff heavy attack recieving standard damage like night maiden's mist).
=== FP Generation ===
Hitting enemies with attacks of all types will restore a small amount of FP. The amount restored is based on your max FP, Intelligence, and whether it was a light, heavy, or critical attack. Slower attacking armaments will also generally restore more FP.
=== Affinities ===
Weapon Affinities/Infusions have been overhauled entirely. Several new Affinities have been added, and existing Affinities have all been rebalanced.
Affinities now grant a variety of passive effects in addition to changing weapon scaling, ranging from slow hpregen from Blessed to reduced armament Weight from Gravitational. 
Affinities no longer completely override weapon scaling, and instead modify it. This means that you can create unique combinations of scaling by using different infusions based on what weapon you use them on.
=== Status Buildup ===
Completely rebalanced the amount of status buildup weapons deal.
Arcane scaling now applies to all status effects, and is applied regardless of a weapon's Arcane damage scaling, up to 1.5x at 99.
Weapon Critical Attacks apply an increased status buildup by 3x of the original value.
Weapons deal less status buildup per individual hit while in a Powerstancing (or paired weapon) configuration, but hitting with both weapons deals slightly more overall.
Attacks that hit multiple times in very quick succession (such as the special Heavy Attack on the Warhawk Talon and Serpentbone Blade) deal greatly reduced status buildup with the initial fast hit, but all hits connecting will deal the weapon's full buildup.
=== UI ===
New UI elements have been added to show off several hidden weapon stats and improve the visual appearance of the stat card. A visual of the overhauled UI can be seen on the right. 
=== Damage Types ===
Changed damage type of the player's gear to better reflect the type of damage that should be used. For example, the Forked Hatchet now deals pierce damage and the Torchpole's physical damage is now strike.
=== Attack Trails ===
Introduced unique attack trails for most weapons. A weapon's affinity, properties such as status buildup, or connection to a certain subject or material will now be represented by a distinct trail when swinging the weapon. Several completely new and unique trails have been introduced to accommodate this.
=== Upgrading Weapons ===
Weapon upgrading has been reworked extensively. Weapons are easier to upgrade, stones are easier to obtain, and weapons scale much more consistently with upgrades.
===Buffing Weapons===
All melee weapons may be buffed through grease items, skills, or spells, even if they are somber, already possess an affinity, or innately have an elemental damage type. 
Only a single buff can be active on a weapon at a time.
• The exceptions to this rule are buffs from Roar skills such as War Cry, and the special boost from Perfect Deflecting. These will not override other weapon buffs.
Buffing an armament with an Elemental or Status Grease, Buff Skill, or Spell will increase that armament's blocking for that Element or Status by 20%.
• Examples: Using Poison Grease will increase poison blocked by 20%. Using Sacred Blade will increase holyguardednegation by 20%. Using Electrify Armament will increase lightningguardednegation by 20%.
Since weapon buffs add at least some amount of flat damage or status buildup, Greases and Weapon Buff effects scale with the class of weapon. Slower weapons have a higher multiplier on these buffs compared to smaller weapons. Very long weapons also get a very slight penalty.

Colossal Swords - x1.15
Colossal Weapons - x1.2
Note: While throwing blades have a value defined, this will only apply to critical attacks or Skills performed with the weapon. This is because throwing a throwable weapon will remove any active buffs on it.
=== Powerstancing & Multi-Weapon Combat ===
Powerstancing and general multi-weapon usage have been given vast improvements to their moveset flexibility. See the main article for details.
The following weapon classes are now powerstancing compatible:
• Axes with Hammers and Flails
• Greataxes with Greathammers
• Colossal Weapons with Colossal Swords
• Curved Greatswords with Greatswords
=== Critical Attacks ===
Globally increased the speed of Critical Attacks against enemies by 20%.
• This simply makes the animations waste less time, and causes little gameplay difference.
Critical Attacks convert all physical attack power of a weapon's damage into true Damage.
• Crits still benefit from weapon buffs and damage increases.
• Similarly, Critical Attacks against the player (such as enemy grabs or player backstabs) convert all physical attack power into true Damage, piercing all armor.
• Critical Attacks after a parry-induced stance break will deal increased damage if the enemy requires more than one parry. This stacks per additional parry.
• Replaced the special invulnerability frames used by Critical Attacks with standard "dodge" invulnerability frames
• This is a technical change that has a variety of effects. Most notably, this means that you can still trigger most effects (such as talisman accumulation or on-proc effects for various Status Effect related tools) during crits, rather than becoming unable to receive them.
• This does not affect the invulnerability to attacks in any way.
• Critical Attacks provide a large amount of attack-based FP restoration and "Accumulation" buildup.
• "Accumulation" refers to effects such as Godskin Swaddling Cloth, Storied Glintstone Amulet, the Assassin fortune stacking poise damage effect, etc. that build up with repeated weapon hits.
Added the ability to perform Critical Attacks with the left handed armament by pressing the Guard + Light Attack input while positioned for a Crit.
Critical Attacks no longer grant enemies total invulnerability, rather reducing all damage they take during the animation by 66%.
• This allows Spirit Ashes, lingering Area of Effect damage, and co-operators to deal damage during critical animations.
Added the ability to perform Critical Attacks with additional weapon categories, using the Nightreign animations. Their default critical modifiers are as follows.
• Whips: 100
• Light Bows: 150
• Bows: 120
• Greatbows: 90
• Small Shields: 110
• Medium Shields: 100
• Greatshields: 90
